### Prerequisites

In this text, we will practice the addition operation. Before proceeding with these exercises, we suggest studying the text *Running Among the Numbers* (<htcite0>), the text *Advancing an Order and the Complement* (<htcite1>) and the game *Carry or Not Carry? (Game)* (<htcite2>).

source.page: Advancing an Order and the Complement

text.text:
### Sun Tzu's (孙子) 5 factors To do the exercises, we recommend using Sun Tzu's 5 factors as follows: - **The law of morale**: Do not do only one exercise. To reinforce your knowledge, practice until you feel more comfortable, and do not practice on just one day. - **Heaven**: Visualize the numbers you are adding as your own body. Every time you add one number to another, visualize whether the result will be the same as the number of fingers you have or whether it will go beyond that count. Try to recreate the additions you are doing here in other scenarios, to reinforce that what you are seeing here is everywhere. - **Earth/Terrain**: For every addition, you will have squares representing the numbers. When numbers involve carrying, in addition to the 10 possible values a result can have (the numbers from 0 to 9), you may also have more squares outside these limits. Therefore, before you start adding two different numbers, evaluate whether a number will be greater or smaller than the complement of the first, and how this affects the result. - **The commander**: As the commander of your learning, you should: - Be benevolent with yourself and with others who do not understand addition yet, and help the other person to learn. - Be honest with yourself and do not allow your confidence to underestimate or overestimate the problem ahead of you. - Respect yourself by remembering that there are different ways to understand math. Discover the way that makes you feel comfortable and follow it. At History Tracers, we will do our best to help you find your road. - Finally, use your wisdom to identify your weaknesses so that you can train them and turn them into your strengths. - Use your sincerity to identify where you have to improve, and do not create barriers because of possible issues. - **Method and Discipline**: Set aside a period of time to train every day, and respect your rest time. ### Practice Exercise Reading about addition is helpful, but practice is essential for true understanding. Below is an addition written vertically, column by column, from the units to the hundreds. In each column the light blue squares are the digit already there; use the up button () and the down button () to add the bottom digit of the second number in light yellow squares. When the ten squares are grouped, the 1 is carried to the next order. Before clicking the buttons, take a look at the complement of the number below and at the squares: the complement tells you how many squares are still missing to reach ten. Then associate the final result with the squares — the group of ten becomes the 1 carried to the next order, and the squares left outside the group are the digit that stays in the column. **Example: 8 + 7.** The column already holds 8 light blue squares, and the 7 of the bottom number is added to them. The complement of 8 to ten is 2, so the first 2 squares close the group of ten (the 1 carried to the next order) and the 5 squares left outside the group are the digit 5:
8 + 7 = 15 When you finish the calculation, you will receive a medal () and can move on to the next problem by clicking the button below:
